correctness.summary: Writing the ratio as A_{i+1}(q)/((1-q)A_i(q)), q=e^{-t}, reduces the problem to Eulerian polynomials. Their recurrence gives simple negative roots, monicity, constant term 1, and no common roots for consecutive polynomials. For every i>=3 the product of root moduli is 1 and degree is at least 2, so A_i has a root r in (-1,0). This becomes a genuine pole at z=-log(-r)-i*pi in Re z>0. A completely monotone function is a Laplace transform and therefore extends holomorphically to Re z>0, yielding a contradiction. The cases i=0,1,2 were expanded explicitly as positive discrete Laplace transforms.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Wei and Guo (2014) explicitly pose the all-index assertion as Conjecture 12. Searches by title, DOI, conjecture number, exact polylogarithm ratios, equivalent Eulerian quotients, and combinations with complete monotonicity, Laplace transforms, poles, and Eulerian zeros did not locate the cutoff i<=2 or the all-i>=3 pole obstruction. Later Eulerian-root literature addresses real-rootedness rather than this conjecture. No specific inaccessible paper was identified as likely prior coverage; differently phrased, unpublished, or poorly indexed coverage remains possible.

value.summary: The result completely settles a named 2014 conjecture: both ratio families are completely monotone exactly for i=0,1,2 and fail for every i>=3. The proof exposes a reusable bridge between Eulerian zero geometry, exponential substitution, and the half-plane holomorphy forced by Laplace-transform representations.
